newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Australian leisure growth seen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Australian leisure growth seen.

text.p: Current high price-earnings ratios and low yields reflect the Australian stock market's expection of strong future earnings growth for leisure companies, Brisbane-based Morgan Stockbroking said.

"The sector is characterised by high price-earnings ratios and low yields underpinning the market's expectation of strong future earnings growth," Morgan analyst Sophie Mitchell said in an overview of three of the sector's biggest players.
Amalgamated Holdings Ltd, Village Roadshow Ltd and soon to be floated Hoyts Cinemas Ltd have announced extensive expansion plans for Australian cinemas, she said.
"All these companies are expected to have significant future earnings growth," Mitchell said.
"Future earnings growth from cinema operations for each of the companies will be primarily sourced from offshore expansion in under-screened markets," she said.
"Amalgamated Holdings is an accumulate, appearing the most undervalued of the three companies," Mitchell said.
"Village Roadshow is rated hold with expectations of strong future earnings appearing to be factored into the current price," she said.
Mitchell recommended investors subscribe to new shares of Hoyts Cinemas - "subscribe to the issue with Hoyts offering the highest dividend yield in the sector and strong demand for shares expected."
The A$2 per share Hoyts offer opened on August 7.
She said Amalgamated had the lowest forecast price earnings ratio for the 1996/97 financial year and appeared to have greater funding flexibility than Hoyts, as did Village Roadshow.
"From a balance sheet perspective, each company needs to maintain strong cashflow and funding flexibility to finance expansion plans," Mitchell said.
Mitchell highlighted all three companies' aggressive expansion plans in Australia over the next three years.
If all development proceeds, then the current market of 1,150 screens will increase to between 1,800 and 1,900 screens including 34 to 41 megaplexes, she said.
"There has to be some concern as to whether the Australian market can justify this size of expansion," Mitchell said.
